 Matas Buzelis delivered 18 points (5-of-9 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), nine rebounds and two assists over 30 minutes to propel the Bulls to a 117-106 win over the Timberwolves on Saturday.
 Buzelis has gotten off to a rocky start overall this season, but he looked sharp in the early stages of this one, pouring in a game-high 14 points on 5-of-6 shooting, including 2-of-3 from beyond the arc, in the opening half. He cooled off considerably afterwards, notching just four points in the entire second half. Still, he managed to do enough as Chicago’s primary offensive creator in place of injured rookie sensation Caleb Wilson, who is set to miss 4-6 weeks with a fractured right hand, to power them to a much-needed road win. It’s hard to trust him for fantasy purposes given how up-and-down he’s been, but he should get plenty of scoring chances while Wilson is sidelined for at least the next month.
 -  George Bissell

 Matas Buzelis lit up the Cavaliers with 23 points (8-of-14 FGs), three rebounds, one steal, one block and three three-pointers on Monday. 
 It was a rough start to the season for Buzelis, but he is starting to pick the production up. This ended up being a new season high for scoring for him, and while he didn’t dish out any dimes, he made up for it with efficient shooting and some defensive production. Buzelis may not live up to preseason expectations, but he should be much better than how he started the season. Chicago will need him to if they want to turn their season around, especially with Caleb Wilson set to miss at least a month. 
 Matas Buzelis

 Forward 
 #14 
 Matas Buzelis finished Wednesday’s loss to the Spurs with 13 points (5-of-12 FGs), three rebounds, two assists and three three-pointers. 
 Unfortunately for those rostering him, Buzelis was unable to build on Sunday’s performance against the 76ers. The field-goal percentage against the Spurs wasn’t terrible, but the Bulls forward racked up a team-high six turnovers. Something to watch in the days to come is the state of Caleb Wilson’s right hand. The rookie forward left Wednesday’s game early in the third quarter after hitting his hand on Victor Wembanyama’s elbow. If Wilson has to miss time, which we hope won’t be the case, that could raise Buzelis’ fantasy ceiling.

 Matas Buzelis recorded 19 points (6-of-10 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, one block and three three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the 76ers. 
 Buzelis has gotten off to a slow start, seemingly struggling to find his place in the Bulls’ offense with Caleb Wilson in the fold. The third-year forward had no such issues on Sunday, shooting 60 percent from the field. Buzelis’ 19 points were his most in a game since October 24, when he scored a season-high 21 against the Wizards. The Bulls play three games next week, starting with the Spurs on Wednesday.

 Matas Buzelis accumulated 17 points (5-of-13 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Knicks. 
 Buzelis is shooting just 38.8 percent from the field this season, seven percentage points lower than his career number. Add in the full stat line, and things could have gone far worse for those rostering Buzelis.

 Matas Buzelis finished Saturday’s loss to the Wizards with 21 points (7-of-13 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, one steal and two three-pointers. 
 Buzelis had a difficult start to the season, totaling 24 points on 4-of-17 shooting. A 13-of-16 night at the foul line in the Bulls’ season-opening loss to the Raptors gave the point total a welcome boost. He was considerably better against the Wizards, shooting over 50 percent from the field and finishing a blocked shot shy of a complete stat line. Given what he’s being asked to do as one of the Bulls’ young building blocks, Buzelis’ field-goal percentage may struggle. That said, he’s still someone who should be rostered in all fantasy leagues.

 Matas Buzelis recorded 19 points (6-of-9 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, three assists, one steal, one block and five three-pointers in Wednesday’s exhibition against the Bucks. 
 Buzelis led six Bulls in double figures on Wednesday, but his three-point shooting stood out. The third-year forward made five of seven attempts. Last season, Buzelis made at least five triples in six games, including a 7-of-8 in a December 21 win over the Hawks. He attempted 6.4 three-pointers per game last season but made just 34.9 percent. If Buzelis becomes a reliable perimeter shooter, his fantasy ceiling will rise considerably.

 Matas Buzelis notched 14 points (6-of-15 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, one assist, two steals and two blocks in Wednesday’s exhibition against the Suns. 
 While he had a rough night from beyond the arc, going 0-of-6, Buzelis did everything else in his first appearance of the preseason. The four defensive contributions were especially encouraging, as he’s coming off a 2025-26 season in which he averaged 0.7 steals and 1.5 blocks per game. If Buzelis can build on that defensive output, he becomes an even more appealing option in category leagues.

 Matas Buzelis (ankle) won’t return to Friday’s game against the Magic.
